external_source_provenance.method: local extracted text plus direct view of all three typeset page images; PDF bytes hashed
external_source_provenance.notation: Algebraic-closure bars and characteristic restrictions are visible in the page images.
external_source_provenance.finding: The Section 2 f3 formula specializes to the literal g1/g2 definition. The theorem concerns algebraic-closure x coordinates on a smooth short-Weierstrass curve in characteristic other than 2 and 3. It supplies no Boolean/digit equivalence or rational-point/DLP recovery.

external_source_provenance.source: Stanley, Smith Normal Form in Combinatorics
external_source_provenance.version: arXiv v2, April 2, 2016; paper dated April 5, 2016
external_source_provenance.method: local extracted text and direct view of all three typeset pages; PDF bytes hashed
external_source_provenance.notation: Read Theorem 2.1(4),(5), Example 2.2 and Theorems 2.3-2.4 with their displayed conventions and proof sketches.
external_source_provenance.finding: Integer Smith form is valid over the PID Z; Example 2.2 prevents assuming it over Z[x]. All-minor gcds follow from full equivalence. The row-cokernel convention and rectangular indexing need explicit adaptation; the protocol correctly uses the m-dimensional codomain and free part Z^(m-r).

external_source_provenance.version: parent acquisition September 9, 2026, exact HTML hash in inventory
external_source_provenance.method: local complete text plus original HTML TeX statements and displayed proofs
external_source_provenance.notation: Minors, codomain indexing, zero-minor conventions and base-change direction retained in raw TeX.
external_source_provenance.finding: Fitting ideals use presentation minors and commute with base change. Applied to the column presentation, Fitt_(m-k)=I_k. These statements require the supplied matrix certificates and do not turn a selected minor into an exact exceptional set.

external_source_provenance.finding: Combining the displayed long exact sequence with the two declared short exact sequences over Z yields the stated kernel-basechange sequence, using freeness of the image. The concrete Av/p class and saturated V-basis remain certificate obligations.

external_source_provenance.source: Caminata and Gorla, Solving degree, last fall degree, and related invariants
external_source_provenance.method: local extracted text and direct view of all nine typeset pages; PDF bytes hashed
external_source_provenance.notation: Read iterative row completion, Definitions 1.3 and 1.5, Example 2.4, Definitions 2.5-2.6 and Theorem 3.1 with its full displayed proof.
external_source_provenance.finding: The bounded iterative closure, first-fall quotient and last/solving degree are distinct objects. Example 2.4 rules out a transient-plateau certificate. Theorem 3.1 assumes a degree-compatible order and iterated closure, so it does not identify the frozen one-shot cokernel with those invariants.
